checks.note: All seven segments are present in all three narrated languages, and the short_clips fact puts the longest narration at 33.92 s (Mandarin segment 6), under the 35 s ceiling; the longest Spanish narration is 31.36 s and the longest English 24 s. The chapter lists in guide-en-desktop.png, guide-es-desktop.png and guide-zh-Hans-desktop.png show seven chapters of 0:10 to 0:36 apiece rather than one 2.5-minute video.

The no_owl fact searched 18 files and found no owl or mascot. In every guide screenshot the four panels are the surgical site and anatomy: the head with the mastoid dressing, hands taking the bandage off, the healed incision behind the ear, and a magnified ear showing the incision and tape strips. Nothing cartoon or character-like appears anywhere a patient looks.

The narrator fact reports one narrator voice per language for all three narrated languages (en, es, zh-Hans). Nothing in any screenshot shows a character speaking at the patient: the video panel is illustrations plus a title card (guide-from-link.png), with no talking figure and no speech bubbles.

The subtitles fact has captions on all seven segments in en, es and zh-Hans. At desktop width the caption band under the video is legible in each language (guide-en-desktop.png, guide-es-desktop.png, guide-zh-Hans-desktop.png), with a Captions / Subtitulos / 字幕 toggle on. At phone width the transcript under the player is the caption track and highlights the spoken word, as intended: guide-en-phone.png, guide-es-phone.png and guide-zh-Hans-phone.png each show the active sentence in full, above the call-for-help bar, with a word highlighted. The Spanish desktop caption band ends at a comma because the sentence is split across cues, not because text is cut.

The toc fact lists seven chapters, and each one landed exactly at its expected start (0, 9.76, 30.56, 54.64, 68.08, 88.16, 114.56 s) with the right chapter going active; every chapter is visible at 1280x800 in all three languages. The desktop screenshots show the full numbered list with per-chapter times in the left rail, and the phone screenshots show a chapter control reading CHAPTER 1 OF 7 / CAPITULO 1 DE 7 / 章节 1 / 7 with a dropdown and prev-next arrows.

The languages fact shows the page, the audio file and the first sentence all matching the chosen language for both es and zh-Hans. The screenshots confirm it end to end: guide-es-desktop.png is Spanish in the title, the language selector, the chapter list, the caption band, the transcript and the call-for-help labels, and even the label inside the illustration reads Revise si hay cinta; guide-zh-Hans-desktop.png is Mandarin throughout with 检查有没有胶布 on the same panel. No English is left behind in either translated view.

The provider_file fact measures 607 ms from paste to link, zero account or login fields, and no network requests after load, so the block is pasted and the link copied in well under a minute with no account and no new app. provider-filled.png shows the table with Antibiotic No, Pain medication Yes, Follow-up 2026-10-01, Language Espanol and Reviewed by Dr. Example 2026-09-19, each marked 'your block'. provider-draft.png shows the same table falling back to presets, each marked 'preset', with a plain 'Lines we could not read' panel saying the presets apply and how to override them, which is the right behaviour for a block whose *** placeholders are still unfilled. The page also states that nothing pasted leaves it and that the link never carries a name.

The review_line fact has exactly one line in the block carrying the review: 'Video guide: language {English/Spanish/Mandarin}    Reviewed by *** on ***'. It reaches the patient: guide-from-link-badges.png, scrolled to the end of the transcript, shows the clinician badge 'Revisado por un profesional de la salud 19 de septiembre de 2026', alongside the honest badges saying the translation and this review are AI and not Song's approval.

The card_summary fact reports the card on the first screen at both desktop and phone, and the card itself returns 200. The link is one tap in every view: 'Print the card' in the desktop header (guide-en-desktop.png) and its translations 'Imprimir la tarjeta' and '打印卡片' in the Spanish and Mandarin headers, and on the phone it sits just under the player controls, above the fold, in all three languages.
